trips.name: Tre Cime & Sorapis
trips.route: Val Fiscalina → Tre Cime → Misurina → Sorapis → Cortina area
trips.summary: The three limestone towers of Tre Cime and the turquoise lake at Sorapis. A proposed hut-to-hut route.
stops: Val Fiscalina → Pian di Cengia area
Pian di Cengia → Tre Cime → Auronzo area
trips.focus: Steep climbs, rocky descents, exposed paths and moving with a hut-to-hut pack.
trips.note: This is a route concept. The final approach and finish need local assessment to create a continuous itinerary without via ferrata. Hut bookings and exposed trail sections must be checked.
trips.distanceNote: 50–60 km is our planning target, not a measured track. The published reference is about 40 km and includes a bus finish; our proposed all-on-foot extension still needs mapping.

photo.alt: The three limestone faces of Tre Cime di Lavaredo above a mountain hut.
photo.author: Frisia Orientalis

trips.name: Mont Blanc · Aiguilles Rouges
trips.summary: Lac Blanc, the Bérard valley and Brévent, with views across to Mont Blanc and its glaciers.
stops: Lac Blanc area → Moëde Anterne area
trips.focus: Steep climbing, controlled descents and moving confidently over rocky ground.
trips.note: An experienced-mountain-runner trip. Hut stages and a qualified local leader must be arranged before confirmation.
trips.distanceNote: About 50 km, based on the established mountain circuit. Our overnight stages are a proposal, not a booked itinerary.

photo.alt: Mont Blanc and Dôme du Goûter seen from the north.
photo.author: Tinelot Wittermans

trips.name: Torres del Paine · W
trips.route: Grey → Paine Grande → French Valley → Base Torres
trips.summary: The granite towers, French Valley and Grey Glacier on the W route through Torres del Paine.
stops: Paine Grande → French Valley → Francés area
trips.focus: Wind exposure, long undulating days and enough energy for consecutive climbs.
trips.note: Exact mileage depends on viewpoints and overnight stops. Refuges, access and transfers are unconfirmed; park conditions may change the route.
trips.distanceNote: The operator’s overview lists about 70 km. Allow roughly 70–85 km depending on the chosen viewpoints and overnight stops; the final track is still to be mapped.

photo.alt: The granite towers of Torres del Paine above the Base Torres viewpoint.
photo.author: Felipedd

trips.name: Laugavegur to Skógafoss
trips.summary: Volcanic hills, lava fields and a pass between glaciers, finishing at Skógafoss.
trips.focus: Pack practice, cold-and-wet preparation and efficient movement on loose terrain.
trips.note: The final day crosses an exposed pass. Hut availability, snow, river conditions and weather determine the final stages.
trips.distanceNote: About 80–83 km for Laugavegur plus Fimmvörðuháls. The trail association’s combined itinerary totals 83 km.

photo.alt: Skógafoss waterfall beneath green cliffs in Iceland.
photo.author: Martin Falbisoner

trips.name: Santa Cruz & Alpamayo
trips.summary: Glacial valleys and lakes below the Cordillera Blanca, with views towards Alpamayo and a crossing of Punta Unión.
trips.focus: Consecutive mountain days, sustained climbs, pack carrying and pacing by effort. Training does not replace acclimatisation.
trips.note: Punta Unión reaches 4,750 m. Allow extra days in the Huaraz area to acclimatise before the trail. This is a hiking-led trip at altitude, with running only where appropriate; the local guide and conditions determine the pace.
trips.distanceNote: Approximately 50 km in the operator’s four-day itinerary, including the Alpamayo viewpoint and Arhuaycocha excursion. Exact mileage depends on the final stops.

photo.alt: The snow-covered pyramid of Alpamayo in Peru.
photo.author: Frank R 1981

trips.name: The Rockwall
trips.route: Paint Pots → Helmet Falls → Floe Lake
trips.summary: Three alpine passes, hanging glaciers and Floe Lake beneath the Rockwall’s limestone cliffs.
stops: Helmet Falls → Rockwall Pass → Tumbling Pass → Numa Creek
Numa Creek → Numa Pass → Floe Lake → Floe Lake trailhead
trips.focus: Long climbs, back-to-back trail days and carrying camping equipment.
trips.note: Backcountry campsites, trail access and commercial arrangements need confirmation. Early snow can affect a September departure; the final dates may move within the late-summer window.
trips.distanceNote: 54 km for the Rockwall as published by Parks Canada. The proposed three-day stages depend on campsite availability.

photo.alt: Floe Lake beneath the cliffs of the Rockwall in Canada.
photo.author: Benfwilliamson

trips.name: Annapurna Sanctuary
trips.route: Ghandruk → Annapurna Base Camp → Jhinu Danda
trips.summary: Villages and forest on the approach to Annapurna’s mountain amphitheatre, beneath Machhapuchhre’s fishtail summit.
stops: Machhapuchhre Base Camp → Annapurna Base Camp → Machhapuchhre Base Camp
trips.focus: Repeated days on steep steps, descending strength and patient pacing. Build endurance for a longer trip; fitness does not replace acclimatisation.
trips.note: Annapurna Base Camp reaches 4,130 m. Eight trail days are an outline, with time for travel and additional acclimatisation held separately. A licensed local guide must assess the ascent schedule and conditions. This is primarily a hiking trip at altitude.
trips.distanceNote: Roughly 70–85 km for an itinerary starting around Ghandruk. Road access, the return route and lodge choices change the distance; the final itinerary still needs mapping.

photo.alt: Machhapuchhre, or Fishtail Mountain, seen from Annapurna Base Camp.
photo.author: Bijay Chaurasia

trips.name: Cradle Mountain · Overland
trips.summary: Cradle Mountain, glacial valleys, ancient rainforest and alpine plateaus on the Overland Track.
trips.focus: Self-sufficient pack carrying, changeable weather and sustained time on your feet.
trips.note: The 65 km plan ends at Narcissus with a booked ferry. Track permits, camping and any commercial permissions must be confirmed.
trips.distanceNote: 65 km to Narcissus; walking around Lake St Clair would add about 17.5 km.

photo.alt: Cradle Mountain above Dove Lake in Tasmania.
photo.author: BennyG3255
